plan.planning_summary: The problem requires optimizing a fixed two-layer topology (one SiO2, one TiO2) on glass to minimize mean reflectance over 450-700 nm. Since the material set is fixed to exactly two options and the layer count is fixed at two, the only distinct strategic axes are the two possible stacking orders: Air/SiO2/TiO2/Glass versus Air/TiO2/SiO2/Glass. These represent fundamentally different impedance matching profiles (low-to-high vs high-to-high transition). Given the constraint of maximum 1 route, the priority axis is the configuration that places the lower-index material (SiO2) adjacent to the air interface, as this is the standard theoretical starting point for broadband antireflection to minimize the initial Fresnel reflection before the high-index layer matches the substrate. The alternative order is a valid physical hypothesis but must be excluded here due to the single-route limit; it would be the candidate for a second round if the first fails to meet the target.

routes.title: Optimization of Low-High Index Stacking Order (Air/SiO2/TiO2/Glass)
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A stacking order with the lower-index material (SiO2) facing the incident medium and the higher-index material (TiO2) adjacent to the glass substrate allows for a broader spectral suppression of reflectance within the 40-160 nm thickness constraints than the reverse order, potentially achieving a mean reflectance below 0.03.
routes.design_principle: Impedance matching theory suggests stepping the refractive index from air (1.0) to substrate (1.52) via intermediate layers minimizes reflection. Placing SiO2 (1.46) first reduces the large air-to-coating index jump, while TiO2 (2.40) acts as a coupling layer to the substrate. The specific thicknesses will be tuned to create destructive interference across the visible band.
routes.proposed_topology: Air / SiO2 (variable thickness) / TiO2 (variable thickness) / Glass (n=1.52)
design_variables: thickness of the SiO2 layer (bounded 40-160 nm)
thickness of the TiO2 layer (bounded 40-160 nm)
soft_objectives: minimize arithmetic mean power reflectance from 450 nm to 700 nm
manufacturing_considerations: layer thickness must be between 40 nm and 160 nm
exactly one layer of each material
theory_basis: Transfer Matrix Method for multilayer interference
Quarter-wave and non-quarter-wave antireflection coating theory
expected_advantages: Reduced surface reflection due to gradual index transition from air
Potential for broad bandwidth minimization via dual-layer interference
known_risks: The fixed thickness bounds (40-160 nm) may prevent reaching the optimal quarter-wave or half-wave conditions for the entire 450-700 nm band
The specific index combination may not allow a mean reflectance below 0.03 with only two layers
routes.execution_request_english: Execute a deterministic Transfer Matrix Method (TMM) optimization for a planar stack consisting of Air (n=1.0), followed by a SiO2 (Gao) layer (lossless, constant n=1.46), followed by a TiO2 (Siefke) layer (lossless, constant n=2.40), on a semi-infinite Glass substrate (lossless, constant n=1.52). The design variables are the thickness of the SiO2 (Gao) layer and the thickness of the TiO2 (Siefke) layer, both constrained to the range [40, 160] nm. The objective is to minimize the arithmetic mean power reflectance for s-polarized light at normal incidence (0 degrees), sampled at 5 nm intervals from 450 nm to 700 nm. Use seed 17 for the optimizer. Allow up to 64 solver evaluations. Report the best found thickness pair, the resulting reflectance spectrum, and the calculated mean reflectance. Do not use RCWA, FDFD, or surrogate models.

unresolved_decisions: Whether the reverse stacking order (Air/TiO2/SiO2/Glass) would yield a superior result if the primary route fails to meet the 0.03 target; this requires a second research round not permitted in the initial single-route execution.
plan.stop_if_all_routes_fail: If the optimized mean reflectance remains above 0.03 after the allowed evaluations, conclude that the two-layer constraint with the specified materials and thickness bounds is insufficient to meet the target, and recommend relaxing the layer count or thickness bounds in a future study.
